references.text: Israel's camp was to be kept clean by sending away anyone who was unclean, in order to preserve the holiness of the camp while the Lord walked among them.
Laws concerning uncleanness related to seminal emission and sexual activity, which required cleansing and waiting until evening.
God promised to walk among His people, which required that the camp be kept holy and clean.
Instructions regarding war against enemies, where the Lord goes with the people into battle, and therefore holiness is required.
After fighting against the Midianites, the warriors had to cleanse themselves and stay outside the camp for seven days because of contact with the dead.
An exhortation to be found without spot or blemish, which reflects the need for purity within the community.
